content.text:
I've submitted the episode. My pick is **index 175 (Fe 0.61, Ni 0.22, V 0.18)**, which gave the highest photocurrent I measured: **7.7e-7 A**.

The budget was 3 photocurrent measurements, and I used all of them:

| Index | Fe / Ni / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 175 | 0.61 / 0.22 / 0.18 | **7.7e-7** |
| 49 | 0.62 / 0.22 / 0.16 | 7.0e-7 |
| 144 | 0.41 / 0.18 / 0.41 (close to FeVO₄) | 4.1e-7 |

- **How I chose:** I first compared a composition near iron vanadate (FeVO₄) with one from the iron-rich corner. The iron-rich one gave almost twice the photocurrent, so I spent the last measurement on index 49, which has slightly more iron. It came out a little lower than 175, so moving further toward iron doesn't seem to help.
- **What I didn't test:** I never measured the vanadium-rich region (about 0.6–0.7 V), even though the library samples it most densely, or the nickel-rich region. The best composition could be in one of those areas.
- **Skipped tools:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so no phases were identified. I also didn't follow the model-based suggestion (index 172). Its predicted value was below what I'd already measured, and it was only a small step from compositions I'd already covered.
